subject: Dedicated throughput safeguard proposal - Skyline Analytics
messages:
From: Markus Vogel <markus.v@skylineanalytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated throughput safeguard proposal

Irene / Dylan —

Thanks for taking a look. We're preparing for a year-end reporting window (Dec 20-31) that will spike inference traffic for our analytics pipelines. We'd like to request a carveout / safeguard for our dedicated GPU pool so transient preemption and standby behavior don't cause tail-latency violations for our SLAs to our customers.

Key numbers:
- baseline sustained throughput: ~220 tokens/s average across producers
- peak bursts: up to 3x sustained for 10–30 minute windows
- tail latency SLO: P99 < 750ms for generation calls at typical prompt sizes (~600 tokens)

Specific asks:
1) Confirmation of reserved GPU isolation during maintenance windows (we need an explicit statement of behavior).
2) Proposal for a priority queue or 'safeguard' carveout so our reserved tokens are not preempted by cloud-level standby scaling.
3) If preemption occurs and causes an SLA miss, what is the crediting methodology and timeline?

I've attached a short simulation (queueing_simulation.log) and a suggested carveout matrix (proposed_safeguard_matrix.xlsx) to illustrate our traffic pattern. Happy to jump on a 30 min call to walk through the numbers.

Regards,
Markus Vogel
Director of Platform Ops
Skyline Analytics

Attachments: proposed_safeguard_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), queueing_simulation.log (text)
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Markus Vogel <markus.v@skylineanalytics.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-02T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput safeguard proposal

Markus —

Thanks for the context and the attachments. This is exactly the kind of information we need to evaluate a bespoke SLA addendum. Quick notes after an initial pass:

- Reserved GPU isolation: our Dedicated offering guarantees capacity allocation, but there are behavioral nuances during platform maintenance and emergency scaling that can introduce short preemption windows. We can document the exact maintenance behavior and add contractual language to clarify guaranteed capacity during scheduled maintenance.

- Safeguard options we can offer (high level):
  * Priority queueing for reserved pools (requests from your tenant preempt other bursts within the same pool).
  * Standby carveout: keep N GPUs pinned for your tenant during specified windows (day-of-week/time-range) for an incremental fee.
  * Graceful draining windows: configure a 5–15 minute advance notify/drain before preemption to allow KV cache snapshotting.

Dylan / Grace — can you run a short internal feasibility check on the pinned-GPU carveout and what incremental cost and inventory impact that would have for the week of Dec 20–31? Also, what telemetry we'd need to measure to trigger crediting if a preemption causes P99 to exceed 750ms.

Markus — are you available for a 30-minute call tomorrow at 10:00am PT to sync on traffic profiles and agree on which safeguard path makes most sense? If not, suggest two slots and we'll accommodate.

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Lead, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: provisional_safeguard_matrix.xlsx (draft)
From: Markus Vogel <markus.v@skylineanalytics.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>, ops@skylineanalytics.com
Date: 2026-12-02T12:25:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput safeguard proposal

Irene —

Tomorrow 10:00am PT works. We'll have our Ops lead (ops@skylineanalytics.com) join. A couple clarifications ahead of the call so you can scope effort: 

- P99 calc: measured over 5-minute rolling windows, 99th percentile across all generation calls from our production producer.
- If pinned GPUs are offered, we need a minimum hold of 72 hours for any carveout to be effective (shorter holds aren't operationally useful for our traffic spikes).
- Crediting: we would expect an SLA crediting formula that maps the percentage of requests exceeding the SLO to credits on committed capacity; prefer a concrete example in your addendum.

I'll also attach a short compliance excerpt that explains why our internal auditors require documented non-preemption guarantees for certain fiscal-batch jobs.

-Markus

Attachment: skyline_audit_excerpt.pdf (pdf)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
To: Markus Vogel <markus.v@skylineanalytics.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-04T16:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput safeguard proposal

On Wed, Dec 2, 2026 at 9:12 AM Markus Vogel <markus.v@skylineanalytics.com> wrote:
> Irene / Dylan —
> 
> Thanks for taking a look. We're preparing for a year-end reporting window (Dec 20-31) that will spike inference traffic for our analytics pipelines...

Markus — quick technical follow-up after our internal review and the call earlier today:

1) Pinning behavior: we can support a 'pinned GPU' carveout for the Dec 20–31 window with a 72-hour minimum commitment as requested. Operationally we'll reserve a discrete node set and exclude them from preemption flows. This will add a 12% premium on top of your committed monthly reserved capacity for the hold period.

2) Priority queue + graceful drain: we will enable request-level priority for your tenant on the reserved set and configure a 10-minute graceful drain before scheduled maintenance. For emergency platform events we can provide best-effort drain but cannot guarantee zero interruption; those cases will be covered by the crediting formula below.

3) Crediting formula (proposal): if P99 > 750ms on your committed generation calls for more than 10 consecutive minutes during the carveout window, credit = min(25%, floor((excess_ms / 1000) * 5% ) ) of the monthly reserved capacity fee, applied as account credit within 30 days. We'll draft examples in the SLA addendum.

4) Telemetry: we'll provide a dedicated metrics dashboard (token throughput, P50/P95/P99, queue depth, preemption events) and a signed Uptime Report at the end of the carveout window for audit.

I'll turn around a first-pass SLA addendum this week and share a redline. Irene / Grace will coordinate commercial terms and finalize the premium.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Principal Systems Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: sla-addendum-draft.docx (for internal review)
